_comment: Three-tier topology over three hosts already scanned, so the multi-hop rule has
something to match. Everything here is DECLARED by us, which is why
findings_to_mulval.py requires this file instead of guessing: no scanner reports
who may reach whom, what account a service runs as, or where an attacker starts.
WHY THE DECLARED REACHABILITY IS NOT THE SCANNING PATH, AND WHY THAT IS FINE.
All three containers sit on one Docker bridge and the scanner reaches all of them
directly; it has to, or there would be no findings to score. The attacker modelled
here reaches only the web tier. Those are different questions. Scan reachability is
an artefact of how the measurement was taken, attacker reachability is a property of
the network being assessed, and conflating them is what makes a consequence score
fiction. Until the segmentation below is enforced in Docker, this file states a
modelled topology rather than an observed one, and any result from it must say so.
THE APP TIER IS AN APACHE INSTANCE. It stands in for an application server because
that is what was scanned; the graph cares about reachability and privilege, not
about what the middle tier is called.
THE SERVICE ACCOUNTS ARE DISTRIBUTION DEFAULTS, NOT MEASUREMENTS. They decide the
privilege the attacker is modelled as gaining, so check them against the running
containers before trusting any number derived from this graph.
